title: Admin Surgeon: micro-run scheduling and guarded short-run execution
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: On-call runbooks are long-running and brittle for simple admin fixes. We need a lightweight, permissioned micro-run scheduler (Admin Surgeon) that expresses small runbook steps as short, guarded tasks that can be scheduled, retried, and audited without spinning full runbook orchestration. Scope: scheduler service + lightweight task descriptor, RBAC gating hooks, per-step dry-run flag, and automatic telemetry/trace generation. Out of scope: full playbook DSL, UI for playbook editing (we will integrate the UI in a follow-up PR).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A new scheduler endpoint accepts micro-run descriptors and returns a task id that can be polled. 2) Tasks execute under configured RBAC context and emit audit events to admin-audit-log. 3) A dry-run mode validates actions without mutation and returns estimated effects. 4) Retries and idempotency keys are respected and visible in telemetry. 5) Integration tests cover permission denial, successful run, and dry-run path.
design_notes: - Task descriptor: JSON with action, target, params, idempotency_key, timeout_ms, dry_run=true/false. - Permission model: map descriptor.action -> required scope; enforce in scheduler via SSO token introspection. - Safety guard: built-in whitelist for high-risk actions (eg. infra-destroy) requiring canary-approved flag. - Telemetry: emit structured events (task.created/task.started/task.finished/task.failed) with token-less identifiers; expose per-customer cost estimate to console. - Execution model: short-lived workers (killed after 30s default) and a queued back-pressure layer to avoid long CPU/GPU holds.
implementation_plan: 1) Schema and contract (API + descriptor) -> PR #1422. 2) Scheduler service (Go) + minimal worker pool + audit hook. 3) RBAC integration: call authz service and fallback to admin-approval queue for high-risk actions. 4) Add dry-run validator that performs static checks and runs sandboxed simulators where available. 5) End-to-end tests and telemetry dashboards. 6) Canary rollout to internal ops team, then broader rollout.
rollout_plan: Phase A (internal): enable for SRE and Oncall team behind feature flag; log all task inputs for 2 weeks. Phase B (pilot): open to support rotation with limited quotas. Phase C (GA): enable for all orgs with default quotas and audit retention policy. Rollback: feature-flag off and scheduled compensating tasks to close dangling jobs.
tests_and_checks: - Unit: descriptor validation, RBAC mapping, idempotency key handling. - Integration: scheduler <-> worker flow, audit log write, retry semantics. - E2E: dry-run vs exec behavior against a sandboxed environment. - Chaos test: worker kill during execution and verify retry/backoff semantics. - Performance: 95th pct latency < 150ms for queue enqueue; end-to-end median < 600ms for simple ops.
notes: Current blockers: need an authz mapping for two new actions (restore-snapshot, quick-rotate-keys). Follow-up: add per-team quota enforcement and UI hooks in console. QA: pair with Solutions Engineering for realistic admin recipes. Postmortem learnings from last incident show mis-attributed long-running runbooks — this micro-run approach should reduce blast radius.
